\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Examples: Results}

\begin{definition}[Strings with an even number of true bits]
\lean{Complexity.evenLang}
\label{Complexity.evenLang}
\leanok
The language consists of all finite Boolean strings containing an even number of true
bits.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Machine for recognizing even parity]
\lean{Complexity.evenScanTM}
\label{Complexity.evenScanTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
Consider the finite Turing machine with no work tapes, Boolean states, and initial state
true. It moves the input head to the right on each input symbol, toggles its state on a
true bit and leaves its state unchanged on a false bit; when it reaches the end of the
input, it outputs its current state and halts.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Parity scan machine prefix invariant]
\lean{Complexity.evenScanTM_prefix}
\label{Complexity.evenScanTM_prefix}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.evenScanTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.inputSymbol_at, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a Boolean string and let $j\le |x|$. After $j$ steps of the even-parity scan
machine started on $x$, its state records whether the prefix of length $j$ contains an
even number of true bits; its input-head position is $j+1$, and its output is empty.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Running time of the parity scan machine]
\lean{Complexity.evenScanTM_decidesInTime}
\label{Complexity.evenScanTM_decidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.evenLang, Complexity.evenScanTM, Complexity.evenScanTM_prefix, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.inputSymbol_at, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean input $x$, the even-parity scan machine halts after exactly $|x|+1$
steps and its output is the single bit indicating whether the number of true bits in $x$
is even.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Even-length parity language is logarithmic-space decidable]
\lean{Complexity.evenLang_mem_LOGSPACE}
\label{Complexity.evenLang_mem_LOGSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.evenLang, Complexity.evenScanTM, Complexity.evenScanTM_decidesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesInSpace_zero_of_k_eq_zero}
\difficulty{3}
The language of Boolean strings containing an even number of true bits is decidable in
logarithmic space: there are a natural-number constant $c$ and a finite Turing machine
such that, on every input $x$, the machine halts with the one-bit output indicating
whether $x$ belongs to that language, using at most $c(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1)$
work-tape cells under the stated space measure.
\end{theorem}
